title: Can lazy B-tree priority queues keep their I/O bounds with stable handles?
formal: Is there a deterministic comparison-based external-memory priority queue with a universal constant c of internal storage at most cB words that satisfies the following bounds for every capacity $N\ge B\ge2$? Starting empty and never holding more than N elements, it uses $O(1+N/B)$ external blocks, supports insertion and handle-based decrease-key in $O(1+\log_B\log_B N)$ worst-case I/Os, and supports extract-min in $O(1+B^{-1}\log_2 N+\log_B\log_B N)$ amortized I/Os. Every handle remains valid until its element is removed. All handle maintenance and lookup costs count. Each logarithm is truncated below at one.
context:
A handle lets an algorithm change a particular queued object after that object has moved. For example, a graph algorithm may keep a reference to a vertex’s queue entry and lower its priority when a better route is discovered. The reference must still identify that entry after other insertions, extractions, and internal rearrangements.

Block transfers make this subtle. Moving $B$ consecutive records between a few blocks can cost only a constant number of I/Os. If each record has a reference stored in a different disk block, repairing those references can cost $\Theta(B)$ I/Os. An analysis of the records alone can therefore miss the operation that dominates the running time.

Adding an indirection table is a possible design choice, not a complete solution. It can keep the caller’s handle stable, but the structure must update the table when entries move and look up the correct location on later decreases. Those accesses can again be scattered. The question requires charging these costs to the same operation bounds.

The December 2025 revision explicitly corrects the conference claim about priority-queue performance. It identifies the cost of external references as unaccounted for and reports logarithmic extract-min cost for the straightforward implementation when every element has a reference.
why: I include this because stable object identity is part of a data structure’s interface, and its cost can conflict with the locality that makes external-memory algorithms fast. The target is specific enough to attack with a representation or a lower bound, while the obstruction also matters for other structures that move records in blocks.
definitions: One I/O transfers B consecutive words between internal and external memory. N is an announced upper bound on the number of live elements, fixed for the operation sequence. Words contain O(log N) bits; keys and handles occupy a constant number of words, and key values are accessed by comparisons. A returned handle must continue identifying the same object after internal relocation. Decrease-key receives a handle and a no-larger priority; extract-min returns and removes an element with minimum priority. All auxiliary tables count toward the space bound. Amortized extract-min cost means that total cost of any legal sequence is bounded by the sum of its stated operation budgets.

progress.text: Eenberg, Larsen, and Yu establish a general external-memory lower bound showing that adding decrease-key can increase priority-queue cost. This is background on the resource tradeoff; it does not resolve the particular handle-sensitive bounds on this card.

The revised Lazy B-Trees paper records the missing pointer cost. Its displayed priority-queue bounds explicitly exclude that cost, and therefore are not a solution to the fully charged interface above.

status_note: Reviewed 10 September 2026. Concrete target derived from the corrected bounds and stated pointer-cost gap; the erratum does not establish impossibility.
review_note: Editorial formulation of the unresolved interface issue in the authors’ erratum, rather than a verbatim numbered conjecture. The revised source takes precedence over the original conference claims. Importance assessment is editorial. The model now explicitly fixes O(B) internal memory and uses an announced capacity N; this avoids leaving the memory parameter unconstrained.

answer_criterion: Construct a deterministic priority queue satisfying every stated operation and space bound with all stable-handle costs charged, or prove that no such structure exists in the fixed external-memory model.

importance.reason: Isolates the cost of stable item handles in an external-memory priority queue; a useful model distinction with more limited scope than general I/O lower bounds.
